name: gameplay-cinema-portal
godot_note: Godot starts on the recorded round (round cinema-start) as gameplay-cinema-start does, and stops its AI robots with the Godot-only ai-stop action.

wall_clock_text./@0#1/@0/time: Game.countTime counts Date seconds; the reference player's Date follows the host clock, not its stepped frames, so TIME reads 178 or 177 here depending on the machine

origin: The robots' effects (checkpoint 5): the round of gameplay-cinema-bomb (AI robots stopped); the reposition fixture puts the player on (3, 3) under the portal at (3, 2); it walks up into it (Portal.runEngine: SendRobotCommand fades the robot's clip, alpha 1 - count / 35: fade, fade-late) and arrives at the other portal (arrive: robotMoveStart makes the clip again, InvincibilityCommand(45) blinks).

actions.godot_note: Godot cannot roll the original's board yet (its Math.random draws before the map are not reproduced): the round this START opens takes its board (every box's _brick5 frame, the layout's hold cells and portals) and the enemy robots from the golden of the cinema-start capture (App.round_as_recorded).
AIControl.stop through the original's own method (fixture); Godot gives the robot no commands, as it then has none.

The reposition fixture puts the player's view on an empty floor cell through the original's setters; Godot puts the player on that cell (Game.reposition_human).

composite_alpha: SendRobotCommand fades the robot clip (alpha compared); Flash applies that alpha to each shape inside the clip, so its overlapping shapes add up (the head stays bluer), while the baked image fades as one: the faded clip is left out of the pixel score.
